blindSummary: The penal code criminalises same-sex conduct (3 years); a 2024 UPR stakeholder report documents violence and discrimination by both state and non-state actors; military government rule since 2021; no legal gender recognition.
blindOutOfScope: Military government rule; documented state and non-state violence.
blindSourceSummaries: An international human-rights organisation: a universal-review stakeholder report covering LGBTIQ+ rights in this country — criminalisation with prison terms and the social context.

A foreign government's 2021 human-rights report on a neighbouring state (about a different country, included in this record's sources): official assessment - same-sex conduct not specifically criminalised but LGBT persons face stigma; no anti-discrimination protections.

A foreign government's 2023 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised via 'indecency'-type penal-code provisions; documents violence and discrimination against LGBT persons and police harassment.

Joint UPR stakeholder report (Oct 2024) by an international human-rights organisation and a co-author, on LGBT+ rights in this country: criminalisation of consensual same-sex activity; police arbitrary arrests, harassment and extortion; a hostile and 'sometimes deadly' environment; widespread stigmatisation hinders reporting of violence.
A foreign government's 2011 human-rights report on this country: documents security-force torture, prison abuse, FGM, and an LGBT section noting criminalisation and societal discrimination.

A foreign government's 2012 human-rights report on a neighbouring state (about a different country, included in this record's sources): documents the 2012 coup, arbitrary killings, torture, impunity - general context; no criminalisation of same-sex conduct.
